name: BURFORD CAPITAL LTD

priced.reason: book method needs rotce_override or final_growth

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That I am refusing the most asymmetric thing in today's ten. If the Taction entitlement is worth even a third of $700M on a probability-weighted basis, that is $233M against an $839M market cap - 28% of the equity - and it is not in tangible book at all. The stock fell 9% over the period containing the verdict, so the market is assigning it close to nothing, and 'the market assigns nothing to a $1.4bn claim' is the shape of a mispricing.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The outcome of Apple's judgment-as-a-matter-of-law motion in the trial court, then the Federal Circuit. Short of that, Burford's own fair-value mark on the Taction asset in the Q3 2026 10-Q - the company marks its claims, so it will state what it thinks this is worth.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Burford's own precedent is visible and it is the strongest fact available: the YPF asset went from $2.6bn to $160.4M on one appellate ruling in March 2026, destroying two-thirds of the company's equity. Also visible, and pointing the same way: management chose to pay 175bp more and grant security on new notes in the same month as the verdict, which is not how a balance sheet about to receive $700M behaves.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Everything that matters. I cannot handicap a patent appeal, and the Q3 10-Q that will carry Burford's own mark on the Taction asset has not been filed. Recording a fair value on a name whose value is a pending Federal Circuit docket would be the 27-green-runs failure in miniature.

what_changed: A genuinely large and genuinely binary event. After the close on 2026-09-25 a jury in Taction Technology, Inc. v. Apple Inc. awarded $5.7 billion, reported as one of the largest patent verdicts in US history; Burford's 2026-09-28 release states its entitlement would be $1.4 billion if paid as is, 'split roughly equally between Burford's balance sheet and its investment funds' - so roughly $700M on balance sheet against an $839M market capitalisation and $685M of tangible book. Burford itself cautions the amount 'is likely to be altered in post-trial and/or appellate proceedings', with Apple's judgment-as-a-matter-of-law motion still to come and 'significant appellate scrutiny of large verdicts' by the Federal Circuit. Separately, 2026-09-14 (item 8.01) announced and 2026-09-17 (items 1.01, 2.03) closed a $300M private offering of 8.000% senior secured notes due 2029, used with cash on hand to redeem the 6.250% 2028 notes in full. Note the market's answer: the shares are DOWN 9% over 21 days through 2026-10-01, a week after a verdict nominally worth 83% of the market cap. The market does not expect it to be collected.
consensus_case: At $3.82 Burford trades at about 1.22x its own reported tangible book of $3.12 a share - a premium, not the 0.36x the brief prints. The market is paying slightly more than liquidation for a litigation-finance balance sheet whose single largest asset was written down 94% in March 2026 when the Second Circuit reversed the $18bn YPF judgment, taking equity attributable to Burford from $2,448.0M to $819.1M in six months. It is also pricing the lenders ahead of the equity: on 2026-09-17 Burford refinanced $400M of 6.250% UNSECURED notes due 2028 into $300M of 8.000% senior SECURED notes due 2029, secured on substantially all the issuer's assets and the stock of subsidiaries. Paying 175bp more and granting security is what a balance sheet looks like when its realisable value is in doubt, and 1.2x tangible book for a book of binary legal claims is not obviously cheap.
base_case_rationale: No valuation is recordable and the engine's gap is entirely defect. This is the FOURTH consecutive appearance of the same unfixed stale-tangible-book bug on this name (2026-09-07, 2026-09-15, 2026-09-22, now 2026-10-02) and the identical tangible_book_per_share of $10.538 has now been served four times. The Q2 10-Q prints both numbers on one line - 'Total Burford Capital Limited equity 819,059 2,448,022' - and justified_pb uses the December figure: ($2,448,022k - $134,020k goodwill) / 219,584,503 shares = $10.538. On equity_now it is ($819,059k - $134,002k) / 219,584,503 = $3.1198, which reconciles exactly to Burford's own disclosed tangible book value per ordinary share of $3.12. Actual price-to-tangible-book is therefore 1.224x against a justified 1.1 - about 11% RICH - not +202.4% cheap, and the 100th-percentile rank of 337 Financials is an artifact. Second, independently disqualifying: the flag unstable_rotce_2.7%_to_28.3% is raised, and per the standing EBC rule an unstable ROTCE disqualifies the model output rather than cautioning about it - here the 28.3% year is net income of $610.5M booked before the YPF reversal, i.e. the very mark that has since been destroyed. Third, and the reason no number is honest even with both fixed: Burford's value now turns on whether a $5.7bn jury verdict survives post-trial motions and the Federal Circuit. Its own YPF history - $2.6bn of carrying value to $160.4M on one appellate ruling - is the best available evidence on how that resolves, and no justified-P/TBV model can price a binary of that size in either direction.
key_risks: The Taction verdict is subject to Apple's JMOL motion and Federal Circuit review; Burford's own YPF experience is a 94% write-down on one appellate ruling
The equity now sits behind $300M of 8.000% senior secured notes secured on substantially all issuer assets and subsidiary stock
Tangible book of $685M is itself a book of fair-value marks on binary legal claims, not realised capital
The engine's inputs on this name have been wrong in the same way for four consecutive appearances and will be wrong again next week
watch_for: Ruling on Apple's judgment-as-a-matter-of-law motion in Taction Technology v. Apple
Burford's own fair-value mark on the Taction entitlement in the Q3 2026 10-Q - the company marks its claims and will state a number
Any further secured issuance, which would say more about the cost of capital than any model
